subject: biology
title: Enzymes in food and household products
key_idea: Enzymes are used in industry because they work on a specific substrate at low temperatures. Pectinase increases the yield of fruit juice, lactase makes lactose-free milk and the enzymes in biological washing powders remove stains.

blocks.text: Pectinase is used to get more juice from fruit.

items: Plant cell walls contain **pectin**, which holds cells together.
**Pectinase** breaks down the pectin in the cell walls.
The fruit breaks down more easily, so more juice is released.
The juice is also clearer, because it contains less cloudy material.
Pectinase breaks down cell walls in fruit.
This increases the volume of juice extracted.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Lactase is used to make milk that people who cannot digest lactose can drink.

items.meaning: The enzyme that breaks lactose down into glucose and galactose.

items: Lactase is added to milk, or the milk is passed over lactase held on beads.
The lactose is broken down into **glucose** and **galactose**.
The milk is now lactose-free and is safe for people who are lactose intolerant.
Glucose and galactose taste sweeter, so less sugar is needed in milk products.
Lactase is specific: it only works on lactose.
A glucose test shows this. Milk gives a positive glucose test after lactase. Sucrose solution does not.
(Supplement) Lactase breaks lactose into glucose and galactose.
Lactase is specific and does not break down sucrose.

blocks.text: Biological washing powders contain enzymes that remove stains from clothes.

items: **Protease** breaks down protein stains such as blood and egg.
**Lipase** breaks down fat and grease stains.
**Amylase** breaks down starch stains such as food spills.
The enzymes work at lower temperatures than normal washing, which saves energy.
Very high temperatures denature the enzymes, so they stop working.

steps: Set the beakers of water to at least three different temperatures
Put the same stained cloth in each beaker
Add the same volume and concentration of washing powder
Measure the stain remaining or the time to remove it

items: The independent variable is the temperature. The dependent variable is the amount of stain left, or the time for the stain to go.
Keep the same type of powder, volume, cloth, stain and time.
Wear goggles and gloves, as enzymes can irritate skin and eyes.
Biological washing powders contain enzymes such as protease and lipase.
Change only the temperature, and measure the stain left or the time taken.

worked_example.question:
A student investigated the effect of lactase on three different liquids: milk, lactose-free milk and sucrose solution.

The student used an indicator to test for the presence of glucose. A sample of each liquid was tested before and after treatment with lactase.

The indicator turned brown in the presence of glucose and stayed blue in its absence.

Results:
- milk: blue before, brown after
- lactose-free milk: brown before, brown after
- sucrose solution: blue before, blue after

Explain the results for the three liquids.
answer_points: Milk: lactase breaks down lactose into glucose, so the indicator turns brown.
Lactose-free milk: it has already been treated with lactase, so glucose is already present.
Sucrose solution: it is not broken down, as it does not contain lactose.
Lactase is specific: lactose only fits into the active site of lactase.
worked_example.tip: Any three score one mark each. Link each result to whether glucose is made.
